observation_summary: The L-infinity norm calculation in both ArrayRealVector and OpenMapRealVector is incorrect. In ArrayRealVector, it incorrectly uses an accumulation operator (+=) instead of an assignment operator (=) when calculating the maximum absolute value. In OpenMapRealVector, it incorrectly sums the values instead of finding the maximum.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a fundamental error in the computational procedure (the algorithm) used to calculate the L-infinity norm. The implementation uses an incorrect accumulation logic (summing values or adding to the max) instead of the correct mathematical definition (finding the maximum of absolute values). This is a procedural error in the method's logic, not a missing guard or a simple initialization error.
evidence_used: bug_report_description: 'the L_infinity norm of a finite dimensional vector is just the max of the absolute value of its entries.'
bug_report_description: 'the implementation in OpenMapRealVector is not even positive semi-definite'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves changing an operator, the root cause is the incorrect procedural logic (summing instead of finding the max) rather than just an incorrect initial value.
The capability exists, but the implementation of the algorithm is flawed. It does not require a design-level change to the class structure, just a correction to the method's internal logic.
